title: Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) Levy (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2018
short_title: Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) Levy (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend existing maritime laws to support the proposed domestic commercial vessel levy, including payment arrangements, exemptions and enforcement for unpaid amounts.
It would let the Australian Maritime Safety Authority (AMSA) suspend or revoke survey certificates, or detain vessels, where levy amounts or instalments remained unpaid.
The substantive amendments would commence with the companion levy legislation, forming part of a three-bill package covering imposition, collection and consequential changes to maritime laws.
changes: Existing provisions directing levy payments to AMSA would be extended to the new levy.
Vessels liable for the new levy would be exempt from the Marine Navigation (Regulatory Functions) Levy.
Certificate suspension or revocation for non-payment would require a show cause notice, with review rights extending to the new decisions.
A vessel detained for non-payment would have to be released when the amount was paid.
summary.affected: Owners and survey certificate holders of leviable domestic commercial vessels, AMSA and marine safety inspectors would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Damian Drum
speeches.brief: The Marine Safety (Domestic Commercial Vessel) Levy (Consequential Amendments) Bill 2018 amends three acts to implement the new levy, expanding AMSA's powers to suspend certificates or detain vessels for nonpayment.
